text:
Alex: Heads up — I want to propose an apples-to-apples benchmark plan to compare streaming vs non-streaming paths end-to-end. Focus areas: kernel selection, batching heuristics, KV cache behavior, and regression signal.
Priya: +1. we need strict controls so differences are attributable to streaming semantics only. :eyes: 
Mateo: Agreed. Can we enumerate the invariants? model binary, quantization, and hardware must be identical.
Jenna: Also same prompt set, same client concurrency pattern, same total token budget per trial.
Alex: Draft invariants: 1) identical model file (SHA256), 2) identical quantization flags, 3) identical GPU type and driver, 4) same seed for synthetic replay harness, 5) warmup period and cache priming step.
Priya: For KV cache behavior we should have two modes: cold-cache (no prefix) and primed-cache (replay with prefixes to fill KV). Run both for streaming & non-streaming.
Mateo: Good call. For batching heuristics: run with 'auto-batch' and 'fixed-batch' configs. Also vary max_batch_tokens and max_batch_requests.
Jenna: We should capture kernel selection traces. Add a profiler flag that logs chosen kernel ids per layer and sequence length distribution.
Alex: Proposed command lines (example):
```
# streaming mode
replay-harness --model /models/gptx-8b.q4 --mode streaming --clients 120 --target-tps 800 \
  --kernel-policy auto --batcher auto --kv-mode primed --warmup 120 

# non-streaming (blocking) mode
replay-harness --model /models/gptx-8b.q4 --mode blocking --clients 120 --target-tps 800 \n  --kernel-policy auto --batcher auto --kv-mode primed --warmup 120
```
Samir: Add a flag to force kernel-policy=static to test a single kernel selection baseline. Useful to isolate kernel switching overhead.
Priya: Metrics to collect (minimum): P50/P90/P95/P99 latency (end-to-end & token-level), tokens/sec, GPU util, SM stall reasons, kernel invocation counts, batch size distribution, KV hit/miss rate.
Mateo: Also collect client-side readloop metrics: average chunk size, time between chunks, backpressure events (# blocked send attempts).
Jenna: For streaming-specific instrumentation: count number of chunked writes per response, measure inter-chunk latency, and record application-level backpressure signals.
LoadBot: Started trial 1769504330: streaming, primed-kv, auto-batch, clients=120.
Alex: Good. Reminder: ensure we pin the same microcode and CUDA version across runs. Small driver diff changed kernel scheduler last quarter and skewed results.
Priya: For apples-to-apples: also disable any adaptive quantization or per-token fallback heuristics that trigger additional kernels.
Samir: On batching heuristics: recommend these settings for the matrix:
- max_batch_tokens: [4096, 8192]
- max_batch_requests: [8, 32]
- batch_timeout_ms: [2, 8, 20]
These will give us latency/throughput tradeoffs.
Mateo: Good sweep. We should do Latin-square ordering to avoid time-of-day infra noise. Randomize order but keep seeds logged.
Jenna: Profiling snippet to include in runtime logs:
```
[profile] layer=14 seq_len=128 kernel_id=0x3f calls=432 time_ms=12.4
[profile] kernel_switch events=17 reason=batch_shape_change
```
Alex: Want to capture tracer timeline traces for a subset of requests (full timeline of kernel launches, cudnn calls, memcpy, host wait). 1 in 1000 sampling should be enough.
Priya: KV priming plan: for primed runs, feed 5k distinct prompts from our replay corpus during warmup, then run measurement window for 10 minutes. For cold runs, skip warmup and start measurement immediately.
Samir: Note: cold runs will spike lower GPU utilization due to smaller effective batch sizes early; we should report utilization over measurement window only.
Jenna: Regression detection rule: compare median tokens/sec and P95 latency; flag if tokens/sec drops >5% or P95 increases >10% vs baseline. Also attach kernel-switch delta metric (# switches per 10k tokens).
Alex: For streaming path testing, we must control client chunking behaviour. Proposed client configs:
- chunk_size_bytes: [512, 2048, 8192]
- client_read_loop_delay_ms: [0, 10, 50]
This will show sensitivity to small vs large chunking and readloop backpressure.
Mateo: Implementation detail: our replay harness supports a --chunk-config JSON. Example: 
```json
{"streaming": true, "chunk_size": 2048, "read_delay_ms": 10}
```
Jenna: Logging format for per-request summary (single-line JSON) so downstream analysis is easy. Example: 
```
{"ts":1769504335, "req_id":"r123", "path":"streaming", "lat_ms":42, "chunks":3, "kernel_switches":2}
```
Priya: Analysis plan: compute deltas between streaming & blocking for the same sweep cell (same batch config + KV mode + kernel policy). Report scatter plots: delta tokens/sec vs delta P95 and a heatmap of kernel_switch_rate.
Samir: Don't forget to include memory pressure signals — OOM retries can change batching. Collect free_memory, active_alloc_count per GPU.
Alex: Admin: we'll run each cell 3x and take median. Schedule: start experiments tomorrow in the afternoon (low traffic window).
Jenna: After runs, if we see regressions, next step is to enable kernel debug logs and reproduce with kernel-policy=static to localize.
LoadBot: Completed trial 1769504402: non-streaming, primed-kv, auto-batch. result: tokens/sec=76k, p95=42ms. Artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/bench/1769504402.tar.gz
Priya: Nice. Please tag artifacts with metadata: model_sha, quant_flags, cuda_version, driver_version, run_seed.
Mateo: One more idea: microbench kernel-only runs where we replay kernel invocation sequences with no NVMe/host interactions to get pure kernel latency baseline. Useful to subtract system noise.
Alex: Great, that's in scope. OK team — let's run the sweep, collect artifacts, and sync tomorrow 10am to review plots. Assign followups: @Priya owns KV priming scripts, @Mateo owns harness changes for chunk configs, @Jenna owns profiler collection, @Samir owns analysis notebooks. :thumbsup:

Alex: Thanks — I'll post a short doc with the exact sweep matrix and links to the scripts.
Priya: Heading into the run. ping me if anything fails.
